regions.text: の第一章にも次のやうに云ってるる。「よしゃ涵命の特別なる不興を被り、或は機母の如き自然の薄過によりこの意志が自家の目的を貫徹すべき能力を全然絞如するともまた鞠躬努力して間且この意志によつて何の避げらるる所もなく残るは唯だ善意志に過きなくてもそれは寶玉の如くその全價催を自己の裏に敷するものとして真に獨り自ら灼燥の光を放つであらう。

quote.translation: In the first chapter of the Principles of Moral Philosophy Kant also says: "Even if, through a special disfavour of fate or the scant provision of a stepmotherly nature, this will should wholly lack the capacity to carry through its purpose, and even if, for all its striving, nothing were accomplished by it and only the good will remained, it would still, like a jewel, shine truly by itself with a brilliant light, as something that holds its whole value within itself."

regions.text: その他なほ運命概念の適用の例を一、二楽げて置かう。

quote.translation: Let me give one or two further examples of how the concept of fate is applied.

regions.text: 「我々は各の瞬間に於て絶割に非合理的なるものに直面して居るのである。

quote.translation: "At each instant we are face to face with the absolutely irrational.

regions.text: 絶對の事實に直面して居るのである、そこでは我々は行為ではなくして感官である、我々はそこに原始的歴史の事實に擻するのであるそれは我々の測命の内容といふべきものである』（週田愛多照、無の白発約限定一八七1一八六頁）。

quote.translation: We are face to face with absolute fact; there we are not act but sense; there we touch the fact of primordial history; it is what should be called the content of our fate" (Nishida Kitarō, The Self-Conscious Determination of Nothingness, pp. 187-188).

regions.text: 「人の力人の働きずべて人間なるものがいつしか終りを告げて、絶對的權威を以て臨む神約實在に吾々がは加と行知節るところがいづこにかなければならぬ。

quote.translation: "There must be somewhere a place where the power of man and the work of man, everything human, at some point comes to an end, and we come up against a divine reality that confronts us with absolute authority.

regions.text: 啓示に際しては、人はあらゆる抵抗もかひ無きものとなり、あらゆる好悪もないがしろにされつつ、全人格を擧げて否應無しに思ぴかかもなき光兵離ひ生のうちに拉し去られる趣がある。

quote.translation: In revelation every resistance becomes vain, every like and dislike is set at nought, and a person is carried off with his whole personality, willy-nilly, into unexpected light, truth, blessedness and life.
For the great religious figures revelation was not necessarily a path they liked or a work they relished.
